404	/****************************************************************************
405	 * Name: esp32s3_getreg
406	 *
407	 * Description:
408	 *   This function may to used to intercept an monitor all register accesses.
409	 *   Clearly this is nothing you would want to do unless you are debugging
410	 *   this driver.
411	 *
412	 * Input Parameters:
413	 *   addr - The register address to read
414	 *
415	 * Returned Value:
416	 *   The value read from the register
417	 *
418	 ****************************************************************************/
419	
420	#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC_REGDEBUG
421	static uint32_t __esp32s3_getreg(const char *func, uint32_t addr)
422	{
423	  static uint32_t prevaddr = 0;
424	  static uint32_t preval   = 0;
425	  static uint32_t count    = 0;
426	
427	  /* Read the value from the register */
428	
429	  uint32_t val = getreg32(addr);
430	
431	  /* Is this the same value that we read from the same register last time?
432	   * Are we polling the register?  If so, suppress some of the output.
433	   */
434	
435	  if (addr == prevaddr && val == preval)
436	    {
437	      if (count == 0xffffffff || ++count > 3)
438	        {
439	          if (count == 4)
440	            {
441	              mcerr("%s: ...\n", func);
442	            }
443	
444	          return val;
445	        }
446	    }
447	
448	  /* No this is a new address or value */
449	
450	  else
451	    {
452	      /* Did we print "..." for the previous value? */
453	
454	      if (count > 3)
455	        {
456	          /* Yes.. then show how many times the value repeated */
457	
458	          mcerr("%s: [repeats %d more times]\n", func, count - 3);
459	        }
460	
461	      /* Save the new address, value, and count */
462	
463	      prevaddr = addr;
464	      preval   = val;
465	      count    = 1;
466	    }
467	
468	  /* Show the register value read */
469	
470	  mcerr("%s: %08x->%08x\n", func, addr, val);
471	  return val;
472	}
473	#endif

505	/****************************************************************************
506	 * Name: esp32s3_ciu_sendcmd
507	 *
508	 * Description:
509	 *   Function to send command to Card interface unit (CIU)
510	 *
511	 * Input Parameters:
512	 *   cmd - The command to be executed
513	 *   arg - The argument to use with the command.
514	 *
515	 * Returned Value:
516	 *   Returns zero on success.  One will be returned on a timeout.
517	 *
518	 ****************************************************************************/
519	
520	static int esp32s3_ciu_sendcmd(uint32_t cmd, uint32_t arg)
521	{
522	  clock_t watchtime;
523	
524	  watchtime = clock_systime_ticks();
525	
526	  while ((esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CMD) & SDMMC_CMD_STARTCMD) != 0)
527	    {
528	      if (watchtime - clock_systime_ticks() > SDCARD_CMDTIMEOUT)
529	        {
530	          mcerr("TMO Timed out (%08X)\n",
531	                esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CMD));
532	          return 1;
533	        }
534	    }
535	
536	  /* Set command arg reg */
537	
538	  cmd |= SDMMC_CMD_STARTCMD | SDMMC_CMD_USE_HOLE;
539	
540	  esp32s3_putreg(arg, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CMDARG);
541	  esp32s3_putreg(cmd, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CMD);
542	
543	  mcinfo("cmd=0x%x arg=0x%x\n", cmd, arg);
544	
545	  return 0;
546	}

725	/****************************************************************************
726	 * Name: esp32s3_eventtimeout
727	 *
728	 * Description:
729	 *   The watchdog timeout setup when the event wait start has expired without
730	 *   any other waited-for event occurring.
731	 *
732	 * Input Parameters:
733	 *   arg    - The argument
734	 *
735	 * Returned Value:
736	 *   None
737	 *
738	 * Assumptions:
739	 *   Always called from the interrupt level with interrupts disabled.
740	 *
741	 ****************************************************************************/
742	
743	static void esp32s3_eventtimeout(wdparm_t arg)
744	{
745	  struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv = (struct esp32s3_dev_s *)arg;
746	
747	  /* There is always race conditions with timer expirations. */
748	
749	  DEBUGASSERT((priv->waitevents & SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT) != 0 ||
750	              priv->wkupevent != 0);
751	
752	  /* Is a data transfer complete event expected? */
753	
754	  if ((priv->waitevents & SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT) != 0)
755	    {
756	      /* Yes.. wake up any waiting threads */
757	
758	      esp32s3_endwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT);
759	      mcerr("Timeout: remaining: %d\n", priv->remaining);
760	    }
761	}

763	/****************************************************************************
764	 * Name: esp32s3_endwait
765	 *
766	 * Description:
767	 *   Wake up a waiting thread if the waited-for event has occurred.
768	 *
769	 * Input Parameters:
770	 *   priv      - An instance of the SDIO device interface
771	 *   wkupevent - The event that caused the wait to end
772	 *
773	 * Returned Value:
774	 *   None
775	 *
776	 * Assumptions:
777	 *   Always called from the interrupt level with interrupts disabled.
778	 *
779	 ****************************************************************************/
780	
781	static void esp32s3_endwait(struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv,
782	                            sdio_eventset_t wkupevent)
783	{
784	  mcinfo("wkupevent=%04x\n", (unsigned)wkupevent);
785	
786	  /* Cancel the watchdog timeout */
787	
788	  wd_cancel(&priv->waitwdog);
789	
790	  /* Disable event-related interrupts */
791	
792	  esp32s3_config_waitints(priv, 0, 0, wkupevent);
793	
794	  /* Wake up the waiting thread */
795	
796	  nxsem_post(&priv->waitsem);
797	}

799	/****************************************************************************
800	 * Name: esp32s3_endtransfer
801	 *
802	 * Description:
803	 *   Terminate a transfer with the provided status.  This function is called
804	 *   only from the SDIO interrupt handler when end-of-transfer conditions
805	 *   are detected.
806	 *
807	 * Input Parameters:
808	 *   priv   - An instance of the SDIO device interface
809	 *   wkupevent - The event that caused the transfer to end
810	 *
811	 * Returned Value:
812	 *   None
813	 *
814	 * Assumptions:
815	 *   Always called from the interrupt level with interrupts disabled.
816	 *
817	 ****************************************************************************/
818	
819	static void esp32s3_endtransfer(struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv,
820	                                sdio_eventset_t wkupevent)
821	{
822	  mcinfo("wkupevent=%04x\n", (unsigned)wkupevent);
823	
824	  /* Disable all transfer related interrupts */
825	
826	  esp32s3_config_xfrints(priv, 0);
827	
828	  /* Clearing pending interrupt status on all transfer related interrupts */
829	
830	  esp32s3_putreg(priv->waitmask, ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
831	
832	  /* Mark the transfer finished */
833	
834	  priv->remaining = 0;
835	
836	  /* Is a thread wait for these data transfer complete events? */
837	
838	  if ((priv->waitevents & wkupevent) != 0)
839	    {
840	      /* Yes.. wake up any waiting threads */
841	
842	      esp32s3_endwait(priv, wkupevent);
843	    }
844	}

846	/****************************************************************************
847	 * Name: esp32s3_interrupt
848	 *
849	 * Description:
850	 *   SDIO interrupt handler
851	 *
852	 * Input Parameters:
853	 *   dev - An instance of the SDIO device interface
854	 *
855	 * Returned Value:
856	 *   None
857	 *
858	 ****************************************************************************/
859	
860	static int esp32s3_interrupt(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
861	{
862	  struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv = arg;
863	  uint32_t enabled;
864	  uint32_t pending;
865	
866	  /* Loop while there are pending interrupts.  Check the SD card status
867	   * register.  Mask out all bits that don't correspond to enabled
868	   * interrupts.  (This depends on the fact that bits are ordered
869	   * the same in both the STA and MASK register).  If there are non-zero
870	   * bits remaining, then we have work to do here.
871	   */
872	
873	  while ((enabled = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_MINTSTS)) != 0)
874	    {
875	      /* Clear pending status */
876	
877	      esp32s3_putreg(enabled, ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
878	
879	#ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_HAVE_CARDDETECT
880	      /* Handle in card detection events ************************************/
881	
882	      if ((enabled & SDMMC_INT_CDET) != 0)
883	        {
884	          sdio_statset_t cdstatus;
885	
886	          /* Update card status */
887	
888	          cdstatus = priv->cdstatus;
889	          if ((esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CDETECT) &
890	              SDMMC_CDETECT_NOTPRESENT(priv->slot)) == 0)
891	            {
892	              priv->cdstatus |= SDIO_STATUS_PRESENT;
893	
894	#ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_HAVE_WRITEPROTECT
895	              if ((esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_WRTPRT) &
896	                  SDMMC_WRTPRT_PROTECTED(priv->slot)) != 0)
897	                {
898	                  priv->cdstatus |= SDIO_STATUS_WRPROTECTED;
899	                }
900	              else
901	#endif
902	                {
903	                  priv->cdstatus &= ~SDIO_STATUS_WRPROTECTED;
904	                }
905	            }
906	          else
907	            {
908	              priv->cdstatus &=
909	                ~(SDIO_STATUS_PRESENT | SDIO_STATUS_WRPROTECTED);
910	            }
911	
912	          mcinfo("cdstatus OLD: %02x NEW: %02x\n", cdstatus, priv->cdstatus);
913	
914	          /* Perform any requested callback if the status has changed */
915	
916	          if (cdstatus != priv->cdstatus)
917	            {
918	              esp32s3_callback(priv);
919	            }
920	        }
921	#endif
922	
923	      /* Handle data transfer events ****************************************/
924	
925	      pending = enabled & priv->xfrmask;
926	      if (pending != 0)
927	        {
928	          /* Handle data request events */
929	
930	          if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_TXDR) != 0)
931	            {
932	              uint32_t status;
933	
934	              /* Transfer data to the TX FIFO */
935	
936	              DEBUGASSERT(priv->wrdir);
937	
938	              for (status = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_STATUS);
939	                   (status & SDMMC_STATUS_FIFOFULL) == 0 &&
940	                   priv->remaining > 0;
941	                   status = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_STATUS))
942	                {
943	                  esp32s3_putreg(*priv->buffer, ESP32S3_SDMMC_DATA);
944	                  priv->buffer++;
945	                  priv->remaining -= 4;
946	                }
947	            }
948	          else if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_RXDR) != 0)
949	            {
950	              uint32_t status;
951	
952	              /* Transfer data from the RX FIFO */
953	
954	              DEBUGASSERT(!priv->wrdir);
955	
956	              for (status = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_STATUS);
957	                   (status & SDMMC_STATUS_FIFOEMPTY) == 0 &&
958	                   priv->remaining > 0;
959	                   status = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_STATUS))
960	                {
961	                  *priv->buffer = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_DATA);
962	                  priv->buffer++;
963	                  priv->remaining -= 4;
964	                }
965	            }
966	
967	          /* Check for transfer errors */
968	
969	          /* Handle data block send/receive CRC failure */
970	
971	          if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_DCRC) != 0)
972	            {
973	              /* Terminate the transfer with an error */
974	
975	              mcerr("ERROR: Data CRC failure, pending=%08x remaining: %d\n",
976	                    pending, priv->remaining);
977	
978	              esp32s3_endtransfer(priv,
979	                                  SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
980	            }
981	
982	          /* Handle data timeout error */
983	
984	          else if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_DRTO) != 0)
985	            {
986	              /* Terminate the transfer with an error */
987	
988	              mcerr("ERROR: Data timeout, pending=%08x remaining: %d\n",
989	                    pending, priv->remaining);
990	
991	              esp32s3_endtransfer(priv,
992	                                  SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT);
993	            }
994	
995	          /* Handle RX FIFO overrun error */
996	
997	          else if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_FRUN) != 0)
998	            {
999	              /* Terminate the transfer with an error */
1000	
1001	              mcerr("ERROR: RX FIFO overrun, pending=%08x remaining: %d\n",
1002	                    pending, priv->remaining);
1003	
1004	              esp32s3_endtransfer(priv,
1005	                                  SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
1006	            }
1007	
1008	          /* Handle TX FIFO underrun error */
1009	
1010	          else if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_FRUN) != 0)
1011	            {
1012	              /* Terminate the transfer with an error */
1013	
1014	              mcerr("ERROR: TX FIFO underrun, pending=%08x remaining: %d\n",
1015	                    pending, priv->remaining);
1016	
1017	              esp32s3_endtransfer(priv,
1018	                                  SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
1019	            }
1020	
1021	          /* Handle start bit error */
1022	
1023	          else if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_SBE) != 0)
1024	            {
1025	              /* Terminate the transfer with an error */
1026	
1027	              mcerr("ERROR: Start bit, pending=%08x remaining: %d\n",
1028	                    pending, priv->remaining);
1029	
1030	              esp32s3_endtransfer(priv,
1031	                                  SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
1032	            }
1033	
1034	          /* Handle data end events.  Note that RXDR may accompany DTO, DTO
1035	           * will be set on received while there is still data in the FIFO.
1036	           * So for the case of receiving, we don't actually even enable the
1037	           * DTO interrupt.
1038	           */
1039	
1040	          else if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_DTO) != 0)
1041	            {
1042	              /* Finish the transfer */
1043	
1044	              esp32s3_endtransfer(priv, SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE);
1045	            }
1046	        }
1047	
1048	      /* Handle wait events *************************************************/
1049	
1050	      pending = enabled & priv->waitmask;
1051	      if (pending != 0)
1052	        {
1053	          /* Is this a response error event? */
1054	
1055	          if ((pending & SDCARD_INT_RESPERR) != 0)
1056	            {
1057	              /* If response errors are enabled, then we must certainly be
1058	               * waiting for a response.
1059	               */
1060	
1061	              DEBUGASSERT((priv->waitevents & SDIOWAIT_RESPONSEDONE) != 0);
1062	
1063	              /* Wake the thread up */
1064	
1065	              mcerr("ERROR: Response error, pending=%08x\n", pending);
1066	              esp32s3_endwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_RESPONSEDONE | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
1067	            }
1068	
1069	          /* Is this a command (plus response) completion event? */
1070	
1071	          else if ((pending & SDMMC_INT_CDONE) != 0)
1072	            {
1073	              /* Yes.. Is their a thread waiting for response done? */
1074	
1075	              if ((priv->waitevents & SDIOWAIT_RESPONSEDONE) != 0)
1076	                {
1077	                  /* Yes.. wake the thread up */
1078	
1079	                  esp32s3_endwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_RESPONSEDONE);
1080	                }
1081	
1082	              /* NO.. Is their a thread waiting for command done? */
1083	
1084	              else if ((priv->waitevents & SDIOWAIT_CMDDONE) != 0)
1085	                {
1086	                  /* Yes.. wake the thread up */
1087	
1088	                  esp32s3_endwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_CMDDONE);
1089	                }
1090	            }
1091	        }
1092	    }
1093	
1094	#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC_DMA
1095	  /* DMA error events *******************************************************/
1096	
1097	  pending = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_IDSTS);
1098	  if ((pending & priv->dmamask) != 0)
1099	    {
1100	      mcerr("ERROR: IDTS=%08lx\n", (unsigned long)pending);
1101	
1102	      /* Clear the pending interrupts */
1103	
1104	      esp32s3_putreg(pending, ESP32S3_SDMMC_IDSTS);
1105	
1106	      /* Abort the transfer */

1150	 * Description:

1161	static void esp32s3_reset(struct sdio_dev_s *dev)
1162	{
1163	  struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv = (struct esp32s3_dev_s *)dev;
1164	  irqstate_t flags;
1165	  uint32_t regval;
1166	
1167	  mcinfo("Resetting...\n");
1168	
1169	  flags = enter_critical_section();
1170	
1171	  /* Reset all blocks */
1172	
1173	  esp32s3_putreg(SDMMC_CTRL_CNTLRRESET | SDMMC_CTRL_FIFORESET |
1174	                 SDMMC_CTRL_DMARESET, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CTRL);
1175	
1176	  while ((esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CTRL) &
1177	         (SDMMC_CTRL_CNTLRRESET | SDMMC_CTRL_FIFORESET |
1178	          SDMMC_CTRL_DMARESET)) != 0)
1179	    {
1180	    }
1181	
1182	  /* Select clock source and init phases */
1183	
1184	  regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLOCK);
1185	  regval &= ~(SDMMC_CLOCK_CLK_SEL_MASK | SDMMC_CLOCK_PHASE_MASK);
1186	  regval |= SDMMC_CLOCK_CLK_SEL_PLL160M;
1187	  regval |= 1 << SDMMC_CLOCK_PHASE_DOUT_SHIFT;
1188	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLOCK);
1189	
1190	  /* Select clock divider
1191	   * Slot N selects clock divider N.
1192	   */
1193	
1194	  regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKSRC);
1195	  regval &= ~SDMMC_CLKSRC_MASK(priv->slot);
1196	  regval |= SDMMC_CLKSRC_CLKDIV(priv->slot, priv->slot);
1197	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKSRC);
1198	
1199	#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC_DMA
1200	  esp32s3_putreg((uint32_t)&priv->dma_desc[0], ESP32S3_SDMMC_DBADDR);
1201	#endif
1202	
1203	  /* Reset data */
1204	
1205	  priv->waitevents = 0;      /* Set of events to be waited for */
1206	  priv->waitmask   = 0;      /* Interrupt enables for event waiting */
1207	  priv->wkupevent  = 0;      /* The event that caused the wakeup */
1208	
1209	  wd_cancel(&priv->waitwdog); /* Cancel any timeouts */
1210	
1211	  /* Interrupt mode data transfer support */
1212	
1213	  priv->buffer     = 0;      /* Address of current R/W buffer */
1214	  priv->remaining  = 0;      /* Number of bytes remaining in the transfer */
1215	  priv->xfrmask    = 0;      /* Interrupt enables for data transfer */
1216	#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC_DMA
1217	  priv->dmamask    = 0;      /* Interrupt enables for DMA transfer */
1218	#endif
1219	
1220	  /* DMA data transfer support */
1221	
1222	  priv->cdstatus   = 0;      /* Card status is unknown */
1223	
1224	  leave_critical_section(flags);
1225	}

1336	static int sdmmc_host_clock_update_command(struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv)
1337	{
1338	  /* Clock update command
1339	   * not a real command; just updates CIU registers
1340	   */
1341	
1342	  uint32_t cmd = SDMMC_CMD_UPDCLOCK | SDMMC_CMD_WAITPREV |
1343	                 SDMMC_CMD_CARD_NUMBER(priv->slot);
1344	  uint32_t regval;
1345	  bool repeat = true;
1346	  int timeout_ms = 100;
1347	  int ret;
1348	
1349	  while (repeat)
1350	    {
1351	      ret = esp32s3_ciu_sendcmd(cmd, 0);
1352	      if (ret)
1353	        {
1354	          return ret;
1355	        }
1356	
1357	      while (timeout_ms)
1358	        {
1359	          regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
1360	          if (regval & SDMMC_INT_HLE)
1361	            {
1362	              esp32s3_putreg(SDMMC_INT_HLE, ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
1363	              break;
1364	            }
1365	
1366	          if ((esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CMD) & SDMMC_CMD_STARTCMD)
1367	              == 0)
1368	            {
1369	              repeat = false;
1370	              break;
1371	            }
1372	
1373	          timeout_ms--;
1374	          up_mdelay(1);
1375	        }
1376	    }
1377	
1378	  return timeout_ms > 0 ? OK : -ETIMEDOUT;
1379	}

1381	static void sdmmc_host_get_clk_dividers(uint32_t freq_khz, int *host_div,
1382	                                        int *card_div)
1383	{
1384	  uint32_t clk_src_freq_hz = BOARD_SDMMC_FREQUENCY;
1385	
1386	  /* Calculate new dividers */
1387	
1388	  if (freq_khz >= 40 * 1000)
1389	    {
1390	      *host_div = 4;       /* 160 MHz / 4 = 40 MHz */
1391	      *card_div = 0;
1392	    }
1393	  else if (freq_khz == 20 * 1000)
1394	    {
1395	      *host_div = 8;       /* 160 MHz / 8 = 20 MHz */
1396	      *card_div = 0;
1397	    }
1398	  else if (freq_khz == 400)
1399	    {
1400	      *host_div = 10;      /* 160 MHz / 10 / (20 * 2) = 400 kHz */
1401	      *card_div = 20;
1402	    }
1403	  else
1404	    {
1405	      /* for custom frequencies use maximum range of host divider (1-16),
1406	       * find the closest <= div. combination
1407	       * if exceeded, combine with the card divider to keep reasonable
1408	       * precision (applies mainly to low frequencies)
1409	       * effective frequency range: 400 kHz - 32 MHz (32.1 - 39.9 MHz cannot
1410	       * be covered with given divider scheme)
1411	       */
1412	
1413	      *host_div = (clk_src_freq_hz) / (freq_khz * 1000);
1414	      if (*host_div > 15)
1415	        {
1416	          *host_div = 2;
1417	          *card_div = (clk_src_freq_hz / 2) / (2 * freq_khz * 1000);
1418	          if (((clk_src_freq_hz / 2) % (2 * freq_khz * 1000)) > 0)
1419	            {
1420	              (*card_div)++;
1421	            }
1422	        }
1423	      else if ((clk_src_freq_hz % (freq_khz * 1000)) > 0)
1424	        {
1425	          (*host_div)++;
1426	        }
1427	    }
1428	}
1429	
1430	static void sdmmc_host_set_clk_div(uint32_t slot, uint32_t host_div,
1431	                                   uint32_t card_div)
1432	{
1433	  irqstate_t flags = enter_critical_section();
1434	
1435	  /* Set frequency to 160MHz / div
1436	   *
1437	   * n: counter resets at div_factor_n.
1438	   * l: negedge when counter equals div_factor_l.
1439	   * h: posedge when counter equals div_factor_h.
1440	   *
1441	   * We set the duty cycle to 1/2
1442	   */
1443	
1444	  ASSERT(host_div > 1 && host_div <= 16);
1445	  int l = host_div - 1;
1446	  int h = host_div / 2 - 1;
1447	  uint32_t regval;
1448	  uint32_t divider;
1449	
1450	  /* Get the divider which is selected in esp32s3_reset() */
1451	
1452	  regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKSRC);
1453	  divider = (regval & SDMMC_CLKSRC_MASK(slot)) >> SDMMC_CLKSRC_SHIFT(slot);
1454	
1455	  /* Set card divider */
1456	
1457	  regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKDIV);
1458	  regval &= ~SDMMC_CLKDIV_MASK(divider);
1459	  regval |= SDMMC_CLKDIV(divider, card_div);
1460	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKDIV);
1461	
1462	  /* Set host_div divider */
1463	
1464	  regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLOCK);
1465	  regval &= ~SDMMC_CLOCK_DIV_FACTOR_MASK;
1466	  regval |= (h << SDMMC_CLOCK_DIV_FACTOR_H_SHIFT)
1467	            & SDMMC_CLOCK_DIV_FACTOR_H_MASK;
1468	  regval |= (l << SDMMC_CLOCK_DIV_FACTOR_L_SHIFT)
1469	            & SDMMC_CLOCK_DIV_FACTOR_L_MASK;
1470	  regval |= (l << SDMMC_CLOCK_DIV_FACTOR_N_SHIFT)
1471	            & SDMMC_CLOCK_DIV_FACTOR_N_MASK;
1472	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLOCK);
1473	
1474	  leave_critical_section(flags);
1475	
1476	  /* Wait for the clock to propagate */
1477	
1478	  up_udelay(10);
1479	}

1481	/****************************************************************************
1482	 * Name: esp32s3_clock
1483	 *
1484	 * Description:
1485	 *   Enable/disable SDIO clocking
1486	 *
1487	 * Input Parameters:
1488	 *   dev  - An instance of the SDIO device interface
1489	 *   rate - Specifies the clocking to use (see enum sdio_clock_e)
1490	 *
1491	 * Returned Value:
1492	 *   None
1493	 *
1494	 ****************************************************************************/
1495	
1496	static void esp32s3_clock(struct sdio_dev_s *dev, enum sdio_clock_e rate)
1497	{
1498	  uint32_t freq_khz;
1499	  uint32_t regval;
1500	  bool clk_en = true;
1501	  int host_div = 0;   /* clock divider of the host (SDMMC.clock) */
1502	  int card_div = 0;   /* 1/2 of card clock divider (SDMMC.clkdiv) */
1503	  struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv = (struct esp32s3_dev_s *)dev;
1504	
1505	  switch (rate)
1506	    {
1507	      /* Disable clocking (with default ID mode divisor) */
1508	
1509	      default:
1510	      case CLOCK_SDIO_DISABLED:
1511	        freq_khz = 400;
1512	        clk_en = false;
1513	        break;
1514	
1515	      /* Enable in initial ID mode clocking (<400KHz) */
1516	
1517	      case CLOCK_IDMODE:
1518	        freq_khz = 400;
1519	        break;
1520	
1521	      /* Enable in MMC normal operation clocking */
1522	
1523	      case CLOCK_MMC_TRANSFER:
1524	        if (esp32s3_capabilities(dev) & SDIO_CAPS_MMC_HS_MODE)
1525	          {
1526	            freq_khz = 40 * 1000;
1527	          }
1528	        else
1529	          {
1530	            freq_khz = 20 * 1000;
1531	          }
1532	        break;
1533	
1534	      /* SD normal operation clocking (wide 4-bit mode) */
1535	
1536	      case CLOCK_SD_TRANSFER_4BIT:
1537	#ifndef CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC_WIDTH_D1_ONLY
1538	        /* TODO: Use higher frequency */
1539	
1540	        freq_khz = 20 * 1000;
1541	        esp32s3_widebus(dev, true);
1542	        break;
1543	#endif
1544	
1545	      /* SD normal operation clocking (narrow 1-bit mode) */
1546	
1547	      case CLOCK_SD_TRANSFER_1BIT:
1548	
1549	        /* TODO: Use higher frequency */
1550	
1551	        freq_khz = 20 * 1000;
1552	        esp32s3_widebus(dev, false);
1553	        break;
1554	    }
1555	
1556	  /* Disable clock first */
1557	
1558	  regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKENA);
1559	  regval &= ~(SDMMC_CLKENA_ENABLE(priv->slot)
1560	              | SDMMC_CLKENA_LOWPOWER(priv->slot));
1561	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKENA);
1562	  if (sdmmc_host_clock_update_command(priv) != OK)
1563	  {
1564	    mcerr("disabling clk failed\n");
1565	    return;
1566	  }
1567	
1568	  /* Program card clock settings, send them to the CIU */
1569	
1570	  sdmmc_host_get_clk_dividers(freq_khz, &host_div, &card_div);
1571	  sdmmc_host_set_clk_div(priv->slot, host_div, card_div);
1572	  if (sdmmc_host_clock_update_command(priv) != OK)
1573	  {
1574	    mcerr("setting clk div failed\n");
1575	    return;
1576	  }
1577	
1578	  /* Re-enable clocks */
1579	
1580	  if (clk_en)
1581	    {
1582	      regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKENA);
1583	      regval |= SDMMC_CLKENA_ENABLE(priv->slot)
1584	                | SDMMC_CLKENA_LOWPOWER(priv->slot);
1585	      esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLKENA);
1586	      if (sdmmc_host_clock_update_command(priv) != OK)
1587	        {
1588	          mcerr("re-enabling clk failed\n");
1589	          return;
1590	        }
1591	    }
1592	
1593	  /* set data timeout to 100ms */
1594	
1595	  if (freq_khz * 100 > (SDMMC_TMOUT_DATA_MASK >> SDMMC_TMOUT_DATA_SHIFT))
1596	    {
1597	      regval = SDMMC_TMOUT_DATA_MASK;
1598	    }
1599	  else
1600	    {
1601	      regval = freq_khz * 100 << SDMMC_TMOUT_DATA_SHIFT;
1602	    }
1603	
1604	  /* always set response timeout to highest value, it's small enough anyway */
1605	
1606	  regval |= SDMMC_TMOUT_RESPONSE_MASK;
1607	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_TMOUT);
1608	}

1666	/****************************************************************************
1667	 * Name: esp32s3_sendcmd
1668	 *
1669	 * Description:
1670	 *   Send the SDIO command
1671	 *
1672	 * Input Parameters:
1673	 *   dev  - An instance of the SDIO device interface
1674	 *   cmd  - The command to send (32-bits, encoded)
1675	 *   arg  - 32-bit argument required with some commands
1676	 *
1677	 * Returned Value:
1678	 *   None
1679	 *
1680	 ****************************************************************************/
1681	
1682	static int esp32s3_sendcmd(struct sdio_dev_s *dev, uint32_t cmd,
1683	                           uint32_t arg)
1684	{
1685	  struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv = (struct esp32s3_dev_s *)dev;
1686	  uint32_t regval = 0;
1687	
1688	  mcinfo("cmd=%04x arg=%04x\n", cmd, arg);
1689	
1690	  if (cmd == MMCSD_CMD12)
1691	    {
1692	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_STOPABORT;
1693	    }
1694	  else if (cmd == MMCSD_CMD0)
1695	    {
1696	      /* The CMD0 needs the SENDINIT CMD */
1697	
1698	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_SENDINIT;
1699	    }
1700	  else
1701	    {
1702	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_WAITPREV;
1703	    }
1704	
1705	  /* Is this a Read/Write Transfer Command ? */
1706	
1707	  if ((cmd & MMCSD_WRDATAXFR) == MMCSD_WRDATAXFR)
1708	    {
1709	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_DATAXFREXPTD | SDMMC_CMD_WRITE;
1710	    }
1711	  else if ((cmd & MMCSD_RDDATAXFR) == MMCSD_RDDATAXFR)
1712	    {
1713	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_DATAXFREXPTD;
1714	    }
1715	
1716	  /* Set WAITRESP bits */
1717	
1718	  switch (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK)
1719	    {

1721	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_NORESPONSE;
1722	      break;
1723	
1724	    case MMCSD_R1B_RESPONSE:
1725	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_RESPCRC;
1726	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_WAITPREV;
1727	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_SHORTRESPONSE;
1728	      break;

1735	    case MMCSD_R1_RESPONSE:

1738	    case MMCSD_R7_RESPONSE:
1739	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_RESPCRC;
1740	      regval |= SDMMC_CMD_SHORTRESPONSE;

1743	    case MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE:

1749	  /* Set the command index */

1751	  regval |= (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) >> MMCSD_CMDIDX_SHIFT;
1752	  regval |= SDMMC_CMD_CARD_NUMBER(priv->slot);

1796	 *   (READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCKS), ACMD51 (SEND_SCR), etc.  Normally,

1820	  DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL && buffer != NULL && nbytes > 0);

1824	   * handler.

1832	   * there are more than 1 words (at least 8 bytes) in the RX FIFO.

1973	/****************************************************************************
1974	 * Name: esp32s3_waitresponse
1975	 *
1976	 * Description:
1977	 *   Poll-wait for the response to the last command to be ready.
1978	 *
1979	 * Input Parameters:
1980	 *   dev  - An instance of the SDIO device interface
1981	 *   cmd  - The command that was sent.  See 32-bit command definitions above.
1982	 *
1983	 * Returned Value:
1984	 *   OK is success; a negated errno on failure
1985	 *
1986	 ****************************************************************************/
1987	
1988	static int esp32s3_waitresponse(struct sdio_dev_s *dev, uint32_t cmd)
1989	{
1990	  int ret = OK;
1991	  volatile int32_t timeout;
1992	  clock_t watchtime;
1993	
1994	  mcinfo("cmd=%04x\n", cmd);
1995	
1996	  switch (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK)
1997	    {
1998	    case MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE:
1999	    case MMCSD_R3_RESPONSE:
2000	    case MMCSD_R7_RESPONSE:
2001	      timeout = SDCARD_CMDTIMEOUT;
2002	      break;
2003	
2004	    case MMCSD_R1_RESPONSE:
2005	    case MMCSD_R1B_RESPONSE:
2006	    case MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE:
2007	    case MMCSD_R4_RESPONSE:
2008	    case MMCSD_R5_RESPONSE:
2009	    case MMCSD_R6_RESPONSE:
2010	      timeout = SDCARD_LONGTIMEOUT;
2011	      break;
2012	
2013	    default:
2014	      return -EINVAL;
2015	    }
2016	
2017	  watchtime = clock_systime_ticks();
2018	
2019	  /* We should wait for CMDDONE, even if there is a response error. */
2020	
2021	  while ((esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS) & SDMMC_INT_CDONE) == 0)
2022	    {
2023	      if (clock_systime_ticks() - watchtime > timeout)
2024	        {
2025	          mcerr("ERROR: Timeout cmd: %04x STA: %08x RINTSTS: %08x\n",
2026	                cmd, esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_STATUS),
2027	                esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS));
2028	
2029	          ret = -ETIMEDOUT;
2030	        }
2031	    }
2032	
2033	  /* Check if there is a response error. */
2034	
2035	  if (esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS) & SDCARD_INT_RESPERR)
2036	    {
2037	      mcerr("ERROR: SDMMC failure cmd: %04x STA: %08x RINTSTS: %08x\n",
2038	            cmd, esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_STATUS),
2039	            esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS));
2040	      ret = -EIO;
2041	    }
2042	
2043	  esp32s3_putreg(SDCARD_CMDDONE_CLEAR, ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
2044	  return ret;
2045	}

2047	/****************************************************************************
2048	 * Name: esp32s3_recvshortcrc
2049	 *
2050	 * Description:
2051	 *   Receive response to SDIO command.  Only the critical payload is
2052	 *   returned -- 32 bits for 48 bit status.  The driver implementation
2053	 *   verifies the correctness of the remaining, non-returned bits (CRCs, CMD
2054	 *   index, etc.).
2055	 *
2056	 * Input Parameters:
2057	 *   dev  - An instance of the SDIO device interface
2058	 *   Rx   - Buffer in which to receive the response
2059	 *
2060	 * Returned Value:
2061	 *   Number of bytes sent on success; a negated errno on failure.  Here a
2062	 *   failure means only a faiure to obtain the requested response (due to
2063	 *   transport problem -- timeout, CRC, etc.).  The implementation only
2064	 *   assures that the response is returned intacta and does not check errors
2065	 *   within the response itself.
2066	 *
2067	 ****************************************************************************/
2068	
2069	static int esp32s3_recvshortcrc(struct sdio_dev_s *dev, uint32_t cmd,
2070	                                uint32_t *rshort)
2071	{
2072	  uint32_t regval;
2073	  int ret = OK;
2074	
2075	  mcinfo("cmd=%04x\n", cmd);
2076	
2077	  /* R1  Command response (48-bit)
2078	   *     47        0               Start bit
2079	   *     46        0               Transmission bit (0=from card)
2080	   *     45:40     bit5   - bit0   Command index (0-63)
2081	   *     39:8      bit31  - bit0   32-bit card status
2082	   *     7:1       bit6   - bit0   CRC7
2083	   *     0         1               End bit
2084	   *
2085	   * R1b Identical to R1 with the additional busy signaling via the data
2086	   *     line.
2087	   *
2088	   * R6  Published RCA Response (48-bit, SD card only)
2089	   *     47        0               Start bit
2090	   *     46        0               Transmission bit (0=from card)
2091	   *     45:40     bit5   - bit0   Command index (0-63)
2092	   *     39:8      bit31  - bit0   32-bit Argument Field, consisting of:
2093	   *                               [31:16] New published RCA of card
2094	   *                               [15:0]  Card status bits {23,22,19,12:0}
2095	   *     7:1       bit6   - bit0   CRC7
2096	   *     0         1               End bit
2097	   */
2098	
2099	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
2100	  if (!rshort)
2101	    {
2102	      mcerr("ERROR: rshort=NULL\n");
2103	      ret = -EINVAL;
2104	    }
2105	
2106	  /* Check that this is the correct response to this command */
2107	
2108	  else if ((cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) != MMCSD_R1_RESPONSE &&
2109	           (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) != MMCSD_R1B_RESPONSE &&
2110	           (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) != MMCSD_R6_RESPONSE)
2111	    {
2112	      mcerr("ERROR: Wrong response CMD=%04x\n", cmd);
2113	      ret = -EINVAL;
2114	    }
2115	  else
2116	#endif
2117	    {
2118	      /* Check if a timeout or CRC error occurred */
2119	
2120	      regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
2121	      if ((regval & SDMMC_INT_RTO) != 0)
2122	        {
2123	          mcerr("ERROR: Command timeout: %08x\n", regval);
2124	          ret = -ETIMEDOUT;
2125	        }
2126	      else if ((regval & SDMMC_INT_RCRC) != 0)
2127	        {
2128	          mcerr("ERROR: CRC failure: %08x\n", regval);
2129	          ret = -EIO;
2130	        }
2131	    }
2132	
2133	  /* Clear all pending message completion events and return the R1/R6
2134	   * response.
2135	   */
2136	
2137	  esp32s3_putreg(SDCARD_RESPDONE_CLEAR | SDCARD_CMDDONE_CLEAR,
2138	                 ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
2139	  *rshort = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RESP0);
2140	  mcinfo("CRC=%04x\n", *rshort);
2141	
2142	  return ret;
2143	}

2305	 *   to help the driver to eliminate race conditions between the command
2306	 *   setup and the subsequent events.
2307	 *
2308	 *   The enabled events persist until either (1) SDIO_WAITENABLE is called
2309	 *   again specifying a different set of wait events, or (2) SDIO_EVENTWAIT
2310	 *   returns.
2311	 *
2312	 * Input Parameters:
2313	 *   dev      - An instance of the SDIO device interface
2314	 *   eventset - A bitset of events to enable or disable (see SDIOWAIT_*
2315	 *              definitions). 0=disable; 1=enable.
2316	 *
2317	 * Returned Value:
2318	 *   None
2319	 *
2320	 ****************************************************************************/
2321	
2322	static void esp32s3_waitenable(struct sdio_dev_s *dev,
2323	                               sdio_eventset_t eventset, uint32_t timeout)
2324	{
2325	  struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv = (struct esp32s3_dev_s *)dev;
2326	  uint32_t waitmask;
2327	
2328	  mcinfo("eventset=%04x\n", (unsigned int)eventset);
2329	  DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL);
2330	
2331	  /* Disable event-related interrupts */
2332	
2333	  esp32s3_config_waitints(priv, 0, 0, 0);
2334	
2335	  /* Select the interrupt mask that will give us the appropriate wakeup
2336	   * interrupts.
2337	   */
2338	
2339	  waitmask = 0;
2340	  if ((eventset & SDIOWAIT_CMDDONE) != 0)
2341	    {
2342	      waitmask |= SDCARD_CMDDONE_MASK;
2343	    }
2344	
2345	  if ((eventset & SDIOWAIT_RESPONSEDONE) != 0)
2346	    {
2347	      waitmask |= SDCARD_RESPDONE_MASK;
2348	    }
2349	
2350	  if ((eventset & SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE) != 0)
2351	    {
2352	      waitmask |= SDCARD_XFRDONE_MASK;
2353	    }
2354	
2355	  /* Enable event-related interrupts */
2356	
2357	  esp32s3_config_waitints(priv, waitmask, eventset, 0);
2358	
2359	  /* Check if the timeout event is specified in the event set */
2360	
2361	  if ((priv->waitevents & SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT) != 0)
2362	    {
2363	      int delay;
2364	      int ret;
2365	
2366	      /* Yes.. Handle a cornercase: The user request a timeout event but
2367	       * with timeout == 0?
2368	       */
2369	
2370	      if (!timeout)
2371	        {
2372	          priv->wkupevent = SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT;
2373	          return;
2374	        }
2375	
2376	      /* Start the watchdog timer */
2377	
2378	      delay = MSEC2TICK(timeout);
2379	      ret   = wd_start(&priv->waitwdog, delay,
2380	                       esp32s3_eventtimeout, (wdparm_t)priv);
2381	      if (ret < 0)
2382	        {
2383	          mcerr("ERROR: wd_start failed: %d\n", ret);
2384	        }
2385	    }
2386	}

2388	/****************************************************************************
2389	 * Name: esp32s3_eventwait
2390	 *
2391	 * Description:
2392	 *   Wait for one of the enabled events to occur (or a timeout).  Note that
2393	 *   all events enabled by SDIO_WAITEVENTS are disabled when
2394	 *   esp32s3_eventwait returns.  SDIO_WAITEVENTS must be called again before
2395	 *   esp32s3_eventwait can be used again.
2396	 *
2397	 * Input Parameters:
2398	 *   dev     - An instance of the SDIO device interface
2399	 *   timeout - Maximum time in milliseconds to wait.  Zero means immediate
2400	 *             timeout with no wait.  The timeout value is ignored if
2401	 *             SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT is not included in the waited-for eventset.
2402	 *
2403	 * Returned Value:
2404	 *   Event set containing the event(s) that ended the wait.  Should always
2405	 *   be non-zero.  All events are disabled after the wait concludes.
2406	 *
2407	 ****************************************************************************/
2408	
2409	static sdio_eventset_t esp32s3_eventwait(struct sdio_dev_s *dev)
2410	{
2411	  struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv = (struct esp32s3_dev_s *)dev;
2412	  sdio_eventset_t wkupevent = 0;
2413	  irqstate_t flags;
2414	  int ret;
2415	
2416	  /* There is a race condition here... the event may have completed before
2417	   * we get here.  In this case waitevents will be zero, but wkupevents will
2418	   * be non-zero (and, hopefully, the semaphore count will also be non-zero.
2419	   */
2420	
2421	  flags = enter_critical_section();
2422	  DEBUGASSERT(priv->waitevents != 0 || priv->wkupevent != 0);
2423	
2424	  /* Loop until the event (or the timeout occurs). Race conditions are
2425	   * avoided by calling esp32s3_waitenable prior to triggering the logic that
2426	   * will cause the wait to terminate.  Under certain race conditions, the
2427	   * waited-for may have already occurred before this function was called!
2428	   */
2429	
2430	  for (; ; )
2431	    {
2432	      /* Wait for an event in event set to occur.  If this the event has
2433	       * already occurred, then the semaphore will already have been
2434	       * incremented and there will be no wait.
2435	       */
2436	
2437	      ret = nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&priv->waitsem);
2438	      if (ret < 0)
2439	        {
2440	          /* Task canceled.  Cancel the wdog -- assuming it was started and
2441	           * return an SDIO error.
2442	           */
2443	
2444	          wd_cancel(&priv->waitwdog);
2445	          wkupevent = SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
2446	          goto out;
2447	        }
2448	
2449	      wkupevent = priv->wkupevent;
2450	
2451	      /* Check if the event has occurred.  When the event has occurred, then
2452	       * evenset will be set to 0 and wkupevent will be set to a nonzero
2453	       * value.
2454	       */
2455	
2456	      if (wkupevent != 0)
2457	        {
2458	          /* Yes... break out of the loop with wkupevent non-zero */
2459	
2460	          break;
2461	        }
2462	    }
2463	
2464	  /* Disable all transfer- and event- related interrupts */
2465	
2466	  esp32s3_disable_allints(priv);
2467	
2468	out:
2469	  leave_critical_section(flags);
2470	
2471	#if defined(CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC_DMA) && defined(CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM)
2472	  if (!esp32s3_ptr_dma_capable(priv->buffer) && priv->dma_buf)
2473	    {
2474	      if (!priv->wrdir && wkupevent == SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE)
2475	        {
2476	          memcpy(priv->buffer, priv->dma_buf, priv->dma_buf_size);
2477	        }
2478	
2479	      kmm_free(priv->dma_buf);
2480	      priv->dma_buf = NULL;
2481	    }
2482	#endif
2483	
2484	  mcinfo("wkupevent=%04x\n", wkupevent);
2485	  return wkupevent;
2486	}

2560	#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC_DMA
2561	static int esp32s3_fill_dma_desc(struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv)
2562	{
2563	  uint32_t ctrl;
2564	  uint32_t maxs;
2565	  int i = 0;
2566	  size_t buflen = priv->remaining;
2567	  uint32_t buffer = (uint32_t)priv->buffer;
2568	
2569	#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM
2570	  if (!esp32s3_ptr_dma_capable(priv->buffer))
2571	    {
2572	      priv->dma_buf = kmm_memalign(16, buflen);
2573	      if (!priv->dma_buf)
2574	        {
2575	          return -ENOMEM;
2576	        }
2577	
2578	      priv->dma_buf_size = buflen;
2579	      buffer = (uint32_t)priv->dma_buf;
2580	
2581	      if (priv->wrdir)
2582	        {
2583	          memcpy(priv->dma_buf, priv->buffer, buflen);
2584	        }
2585	    }
2586	#endif
2587	
2588	  /* Setup DMA list */
2589	
2590	  while (buflen > 0)
2591	    {
2592	      /* Limit size of the transfer to maximum buffer size */
2593	
2594	      maxs = buflen;
2595	
2596	      if (maxs > MCI_DMADES1_MAXTR)
2597	        {
2598	          maxs = MCI_DMADES1_MAXTR;
2599	        }
2600	
2601	      buflen -= maxs;
2602	
2603	      /* Set buffer size */
2604	
2605	      priv->dma_desc[i].des1 = MCI_DMADES1_BS1(maxs);
2606	
2607	      /* Setup buffer address (chained) */
2608	
2609	      priv->dma_desc[i].des2 = buffer + (i * MCI_DMADES1_MAXTR);
2610	
2611	      /* Setup basic control */
2612	
2613	      ctrl = MCI_DMADES0_OWN | MCI_DMADES0_CH;
2614	
2615	      if (i == 0)
2616	        {
2617	          ctrl |= MCI_DMADES0_FS; /* First DMA buffer */
2618	        }
2619	
2620	      /* No more data?  Then this is the last descriptor */
2621	
2622	      if (buflen == 0)
2623	        {
2624	          ctrl |= MCI_DMADES0_LD;
2625	          priv->dma_desc[i].des3 = 0;
2626	        }
2627	      else
2628	        {
2629	          ctrl |= MCI_DMADES0_DIC;
2630	          priv->dma_desc[i].des3 = (uint32_t)&priv->dma_desc[i + 1];
2631	        }
2632	
2633	      priv->dma_desc[i].des0 = ctrl;
2634	      i++;
2635	    }
2636	
2637	  DEBUGASSERT(i < NUM_DMA_DESCRIPTORS);
2638	
2639	  return 0;
2640	}

2644	 * Name: esp32s3_dmarecvsetup
2645	 *
2646	 * Description:
2647	 *   Setup to perform a read DMA.  If the processor supports a data cache,
2648	 *   then this method will also make sure that the contents of the DMA memory
2649	 *   and the data cache are coherent.  For read transfers this may mean
2650	 *   invalidating the data cache.
2651	 *
2652	 * Input Parameters:
2653	 *   dev    - An instance of the SDIO device interface
2654	 *   buffer - The memory to DMA from
2655	 *   buflen - The size of the DMA transfer in bytes

2667	  uint32_t regval;
2668	
2669	  /* Don't bother with DMA if the entire transfer will fit in the RX FIFO or
2670	   * if we do not have a 4-bit wide bus.
2671	   */
2672	
2673	  DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL);
2674	
2675	  DEBUGASSERT(buffer != NULL && buflen > 0 && ((uint32_t)buffer & 3) == 0);
2676	
2677	  /* Save the destination buffer information for use by the interrupt
2678	   * handler.
2679	   */

2681	  priv->buffer    = (uint32_t *)buffer;
2682	  priv->remaining = buflen;
2683	  priv->wrdir     = false;

2685	  /* Setup DMA list */
2686	
2687	  if (esp32s3_fill_dma_desc(priv))
2688	    {
2689	      return -ENOMEM;
2690	    }
2691	
2692	  /* Flush ints before we start */
2693	
2694	  esp32s3_putreg(SDCARD_TRANSFER_ALL, ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);

2696	  /* Enable internal DMA, burst size of 4, fixed burst */
2697	
2698	  regval  = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_CTRL);

2700	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_CTRL);
2701	
2702	  regval = SDMMC_BMOD_DE | SDMMC_BMOD_FB;
2703	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_SDMMC_BMOD);

2705	  esp32s3_putreg(1, ESP32S3_SDMMC_PLDMND);

2785	/****************************************************************************
2786	 * Name: esp32s3_callback
2787	 *
2788	 * Description:
2789	 *   Perform callback.
2790	 *
2791	 * Assumptions:
2792	 *   This function does not execute in the context of an interrupt handler.
2793	 *   It may be invoked on any user thread or scheduled on the work thread
2794	 *   from an interrupt handler.
2795	 *
2796	 ****************************************************************************/
2797	
2798	static void esp32s3_callback(void *arg)
2799	{
2800	  struct esp32s3_dev_s *priv = (struct esp32s3_dev_s *)arg;
2801	
2802	  /* Is a callback registered? */
2803	
2804	  DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL);
2805	  mcinfo("Callback %p(%p) cbevents: %02x cdstatus: %02x\n",
2806	         priv->callback, priv->cbarg, priv->cbevents, priv->cdstatus);
2807	
2808	  if (priv->callback)
2809	    {
2810	      /* Yes.. Check for enabled callback events */
2811	
2812	      if ((priv->cdstatus & SDIO_STATUS_PRESENT) != 0)
2813	        {
2814	          /* Media is present.  Is the media inserted event enabled? */
2815	
2816	          if ((priv->cbevents & SDIOMEDIA_INSERTED) == 0)
2817	            {
2818	              /* No... return without performing the callback */
2819	
2820	              return;
2821	            }
2822	        }
2823	      else
2824	        {
2825	          /* Media is not present.  Is the media eject event enabled? */
2826	
2827	          if ((priv->cbevents & SDIOMEDIA_EJECTED) == 0)
2828	            {
2829	              /* No... return without performing the callback */
2830	
2831	              return;
2832	            }
2833	        }
2834	
2835	      /* Perform the callback, disabling further callbacks.  Of course, the
2836	       * the callback can (and probably should) re-enable callbacks.
2837	       */
2838	
2839	      priv->cbevents = 0;
2840	
2841	      /* Callbacks cannot be performed in the context of an interrupt
2842	       * handler.  If we are in an interrupt handler, then queue the
2843	       * callback to be performed later on the work thread.
2844	       */
2845	
2846	      if (up_interrupt_context())
2847	        {
2848	          /* Yes.. queue it */
2849	
2850	           mcinfo("Queuing callback to %p(%p)\n",
2851	                  priv->callback, priv->cbarg);
2852	           work_queue(HPWORK, &priv->cbwork, priv->callback,
2853	                      priv->cbarg, 0);
2854	        }
2855	      else
2856	        {
2857	          /* No.. then just call the callback here */
2858	
2859	          mcinfo("Callback to %p(%p)\n", priv->callback, priv->cbarg);
2860	          priv->callback(priv->cbarg);
2861	        }
2862	    }
2863	}

Key findings:

1. **Same SDMMC IP core**: Both P4 and S3 use the same DesignWare SDMMC controller IP (Synopsys DWCMSHC). The register structure (`sdmmc_dev_t`) is essentially the same - ctrl, cmd, cmdarg, mintsts, rintsts, etc.

2. **DMA descriptor difference**:   - S3: `sdmmc_desc_t` is 16 bytes (4 uint32_t fields)
   - P4: `sdmmc_desc_t` is 64 bytes (includes `reserved[12]` for cache alignment - P4 has L1 cache with 64B cache line)

3. **Clock/Reset system is completely different**:
   - S3: Uses `SYSTEM.perip_clk_en1.sdio_host_clk_en` and `hw->clock.clk_sel` for clock source selection (PLL160M or XTAL)
   - P4: Uses `HP_SYS_CLKRST.soc_clk_ctrl1.reg_sdmmc_sys_clk_en` and `HP_SYS_CLKRST.peri_clk_ctrl01.reg_sdio_ls_clk_src_sel` for clock configuration, with additional support for SDIO 200M clock source - P4 also has SDIO PLL support with PMU registers for control, and uses an external clock edge configuration system through `HP_SYS_CLKRST.peri_clk_ctrl02` instead of the hardware register approach

4. **GPIO Matrix / Pin configuration**:
   - S3: Uses `esp32s3_configgpio()` and `esp32s3_gpio_matrix_in/out()` with GPIO Matrix signal indices (e.g., `SDHOST_CCLK_OUT_1_IDX`)
   - P4: Uses IOMUX for slot 0 (direct pin mapping) and GPIO Matrix for slot 1, with different signal naming conventions (e.g., `SD_CARD_CCLK_2_PAD_OUT_IDX`)

5. **Register field naming differences** in `sdmmc_struct.h`:
   - S3: `hw->clock.clk_sel`, `hw->clock.div_factor_h/l/n`, `hw->clock.phase_din/dout/core`
   - P4: Clock control is external (via `HP_SYS_CLKRST`), and `hw->clk_edge_sel` is used for delay line configuration - S3: `hw->cdetect.cards`, `hw->clkena.cclk_enable`
   - P4: `hw->cdetect.card_detect_n`, `hw->clkena.cclk_enable`

6. **NuttX lower-half driver (`esp32s3_sdmmc.c`)**:
   - Directly accesses registers via `ESP32S3_SDMMC_*` base address macros
   - Uses `esp32s3_configgpio()` / `esp32s3_gpio_matrix_in/out()` for pin mux - Uses `esp32s3_setup_irq()` / `irq_attach()` for interrupt setup - Clock configuration is done through direct register manipulation of SDMMC_CLOCK, SDMMC_CLKSRC, SDMMC_CLKDIV, SDMMC_CLKENA registers (all inside the SDMMC peripheral)
   - All register offsets and bit definitions come from `hardware/esp32s3_sdmmc.h`

Now looking at whether the S3 driver can be reused on P4. The answer is no—the hardware abstraction layers are fundamentally incompatible. P4 moves clock management to the system-level `HP_SYS_CLKRST` registers instead of keeping them in the SDMMC peripheral, so the register access patterns don't match at all.

The GPIO APIs differ too, with P4 using different function names and signal indices. The DMA descriptor structure is also different: P4 needs 64-byte cache-aligned descriptors versus S3's 16-byte ones, which affects how DMA buffers are set up. The interrupt controller APIs are architecture-specific as well—S3 uses Xtensa while P4 uses RISC-V with different IRQ attachment methods. Even the register field names in the sdmmc_struct.h header have diverged between the two chips.

That said, there's definitely room to reuse the overall design and control flow since both use the same underlying SDMMC IP. The command building, response handling, DMA descriptor chain logic, interrupt state machine, and event/callback patterns can all be adapted rather than rewritten from scratch.

The sdmmc_ll.h functions are chip-specific, but they share the same API surface, so the higher-level code just needs to swap in the appropriate LL functions. The hal layer code is already fully reusable since sdmmc_hal.c is completely shared. The interrupt event handling logic from the NuttX driver can be ported with minimal changes too—mostly just updating the register access patterns.

## ESP32-P4 vs ESP32-S3 SDMMC/SDIO 驱动差异分析

### 1. 底层硬件 IP 核心：**完全相同**

P4 和 S3 都使用 Synopsys DWCMSHC (DesignWare SD/MMC Host Controller) IP。核心寄存器布局（`sdmmc_dev_t` 结构体）基本一致：
- `ctrl`, `cmd`, `cmdarg`, `mintsts`, `rintsts`, `status`, `ctype`, `blksiz`, `bytcnt`, `tmout`, `clkdiv`, `clkena`, `bmod`, `dbaddr`, `idsts`, `idinten` 等寄存器在两者上都存在
- DMA 引擎、FIFO、中断机制的**功能逻辑完全相同**
- 中断位定义（`SDMMC_LL_EVENT_*`）在两者之间**完全一致**

### 2. 关键差异点

#### 2.1 时钟/复位系统 — **完全不同的寄存器域**

这是**最大的差异**。S3 的时钟配置在 SDMMC 外设内部寄存器中，而 P4 将时钟控制移到了系统级 `HP_SYS_CLKRST` 寄存器：

| 功能 | S3 (sdmmc_ll.h) | P4 (sdmmc_ll.h) |
|------|-----------------|-----------------|
| 使能总线时钟 | `SYSTEM.perip_clk_en1.sdio_host_clk_en` | `HP_SYS_CLKRST.soc_clk_ctrl1.reg_sdmmc_sys_clk_en` |
| 复位模块 | `SYSTEM.perip_rst_en1.sdio_host_rst` | `LP_AON_CLKRST.hp_sdmmc_emac_rst_ctrl.rst_en_sdmmc` |
| 选择时钟源 | `hw->clock.clk_sel` (PLL160M=1, XTAL=0) | `HP_SYS_CLKRST.peri_clk_ctrl01.reg_sdio_ls_clk_src_sel` (PLL160M=0, SDIO_200M=1) |
| 设置分频 | `hw->clock.div_factor_h/l/n` | `HP_SYS_CLKRST.peri_clk_ctrl02.reg_sdio_ls_clk_edge_h/n/l` |
| 相位延迟 | `hw->clock.phase_din/dout/core` | `HP_SYS_CLKRST.peri_clk_ctrl02.reg_sdio_ls_{drv,sam,slf}_clk_edge_sel` |
| **SDIO PLL** | ❌ 不支持 | ✅ 通过 PMU 寄存器控制 `sdmmc_ll_enable_sdio_pll()` |
| 高速模式 | 无 | `HP_SYS_CLKRST.peri_clk_ctrl01.reg_sdio_hs_mode` |
| DLL 延迟线 | ❌ 不支持 | ✅ `SDMMC.dll_clk_conf.dll_cclk_in_{sam,drv}_phase` |

P4 额外有 `SDMMC_LL_DELAY_PHASE_SUPPORTED=1` 和 `SDMMC_LL_SDIO_PLL_SUPPORTED=1`，S3 都是 0。

#### 2.2 DMA 描述符 — **缓存对齐差异**

```c
// S3: 16 字节
typedef struct sdmmc_desc_s {
    uint32_t des0;      // 控制和状态
    uint32_t des1;      // buffer size
    void*    buffer1_ptr;
    void*    next_desc_ptr;
} sdmmc_desc_t;  // sizeof == 16

// P4: 64 字节 (L1 Cache 64B 对齐)
typedef struct sdmmc_desc_s {
    // ... 同上 4 个字段 ...
    uint32_t reserved[12];  // 填充到 64 字节
} sdmmc_desc_t;  // sizeof == 64
```

**影响**：NuttX S3 驱动中的 DMA 描述符数组大小计算和内存布局必须修改。P4 需要 cache-aligned 的 DMA 描述符以避免 cache coherency 问题。

#### 2.3 GPIO/引脚配置 — **API 和信号索引不同**

- S3 使用 `esp32s3_configgpio()` + `esp32s3_gpio_matrix_in/out()`，信号索引如 `SDHOST_CCLK_OUT_1_IDX`
- P4 使用 `esp_gpio_configure()` + 不同的信号索引命名（如 `SD_CARD_CCLK_2_PAD_OUT_IDX`）
- P4 的 slot 0 使用 IOMUX 直连，slot 1 使用 GPIO Matrix；S3 的两个 slot 都使用 GPIO Matrix

#### 2.4 `sdmmc_struct.h` 寄存器字段命名差异

尽管底层 IP 相同，P4 的寄存器字段命名有些变化：

| 寄存器 | S3 字段名 | P4 字段名 |
|--------|----------|----------|
| tmout | `hw->tmout.data`, `hw->tmout.response` | `hw->tmout.data_timeout`, `hw->tmout.response_timeout` |
| cdetect | `hw->cdetect.cards` | `hw->cdetect.card_detect_n` |
| wrtprt | `hw->wrtprt.cards` | `hw->wrtprt.write_protect` |
| clkena | `HAL_FORCE_READ_U32_REG_FIELD(hw->clkena, cclk_enable)` | `hw->clkena.cclk_enable` (直接访问) |
| clkdiv | `HAL_FORCE_MODIFY_U32_REG_FIELD(hw->clkdiv, div0, ...)` | `HAL_FORCE_MODIFY_U32_REG_FIELD(hw->clkdiv, clk_divider0, ...)` |
| uhs | `hw->uhs.volt` | `hw->uhs.volt` (相同) |
| emmcddr | `hw->emmc_ddr_reg` | `hw->emmcddr.halfstartbit_reg` |

#### 2.5 中断/IRQ — **架构差异**

- S3: Xtensa 架构，使用 `esp32s3_setup_irq()` + `esp32s3_irq.h`
- P4: RISC-V 架构，使用 `esp_riscv_intr.h` + 不同的 IRQ 号和配置方式

### 3. 可复用性分析

#### ✅ 完全可复用（无需修改）
- `sdmmc_hal.c` — **完全通用**，一行代码搞定：`hal->dev = SDMMC_LL_GET_HW(0)`
- `sdmmc_hal.h` — **完全通用**，`sdmmc_hal_context_t` 结构体不依赖芯片
- `sdmmc_periph.h` — **完全通用**，`sdmmc_slot_info_t` / `sdmmc_slot_io_info_t` 结构体定义不依赖芯片

#### ✅ 结构可复用（需替换芯片特定函数调用）
- `sdmmc_ll.h` 中的函数 — **API 完全相同**，实现不同。所有 `sdmmc_ll_*` 函数签名一致，上层代码只需 include 正确的 `sdmmc_ll.h` 即可
- `sdmmc_periph.c` — **结构完全相同**，只需替换信号索引宏名

#### ⚠️ 可参考但需大量修改
- `esp32s3_sdmmc.c` (NuttX lower-half) — **控制流/状态机可复用**，但以下部分必须重写：
  1. **时钟配置**：S3 直接操作 `ESP32S3_SDMMC_CLOCK/CLKSRC/CLKDIV/CLKENA` 寄存器；P4 必须通过 `HP_SYS_CLKRST` 外部寄存器
  2. **DMA 描述符**：结构体大小从 16B 改为 64B，`NUM_DMA_DESCRIPTORS` 计算需调整
  3. **GPIO 配置**：替换 `esp32s3_configgpio()` → `esp_gpio_configure()`，替换信号索引
  4. **中断配置**：替换 Xtensa IRQ API → RISC-V IRQ API
  5. **系统时钟/复位**：替换 `SYSTEM_PERIP_CLK_EN1_REG` → `HP_SYS_CLKRST` 系列寄存器
  6. **所有寄存器地址宏**：`ESP32S3_SDMMC_*` → ESP32P4 对应的基地址宏

### 4. 结论

**S3 的 NuttX SDMMC 驱动不能直接用在 P4 上**，但可以作为**非常好的参考模板**。核心的 SDMMC 控制逻辑（命令发送、响应接收、DMA 传输、中断处理状态机）可以直接复用设计思路，主要工作量在于：

1. **时钟系统适配**（最大工作量）：P4 的时钟树完全不同于 S3，需要参考 `sdmmc_ll.h` 中 P4 的实现来写
2. **DMA 描述符适配**：考虑 cache line 对齐
3. **GPIO/IRQ 适配**：相对简单的替换工作
4. **寄存器字段名适配**：`sdmmc_struct.h` 中字段名有差异，需要逐一核对

**最佳策略**：基于 S3 驱动的控制流框架，使用 P4 的 `sdmmc_ll.h` 中的函数来操作硬件，而不是像 S3 驱动那样直接读写寄存器。这样可以最大限度地复用 HAL 层已经封装好的差异处理。
